plants.name: Prunus yedoensis
plants.description: A deciduous tree that produces clouds of delicate, slightly fragrant blossoms before its leaves emerge. Flowers appear in clusters of five-petaled blooms that fade from pale pink to nearly white. It is the most widely planted cherry in Japan and in many temperate parks worldwide.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to early April in Japan; as early as mid-March in warmer parts of its range
plants.location: Japan, Korea, Washington D.C. (USA), and temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: Nearly all Yoshino cherries are clones propagated by grafting, so trees across a region often bloom in near-perfect synchrony, which is why the Japan Meteorological Agency can forecast a single 'cherry blossom front' moving north.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with grey-green strap-like leaves and nodding flowers that have pale yellow outer petals and a deeper yellow trumpet. It grows in meadows, open woodlands, and grassy banks, and is the parent of many garden daffodil cultivars.
plants.location: Western Europe, including England, Wales, France, and Spain; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: Daffodils contain the alkaloid galantamine, which has been developed into a medication used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Magnolia x soulangeana
plants.description: A small deciduous tree or large shrub bearing large, goblet-shaped flowers on bare branches in early spring. The tulip-like blooms are white inside and pink to purple on the outside. It is a hybrid popular in gardens and street plantings.
plants.location: Cultivated across Europe, the southern and eastern United States, and temperate Asia
plants.funFact: This hybrid was first bred in France in the 1820s by Étienne Soulange-Bodin, a retired cavalry officer, and magnolias belong to one of the oldest flowering plant lineages, predating bees.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the genus Protea, up to 30 cm across. The bloom is a cluster of tiny flowers surrounded by showy, petal-like pink bracts. It thrives in the nutrient-poor, fire-prone fynbos landscapes of South Africa.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peak flowering in late summer to early spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with blooms present in March in some areas
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The King Protea is South Africa's national flower, and its thick underground lignotuber lets it resprout after bushfires.
